newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL AND MAN UTD TOPPLE LONDON CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL AND MAN UTD TOPPLE LONDON CHALLENGE.

text.p: Liverpool and Manchester United resisted the challenges of London rivals West Ham and Tottenham on Sunday as they cemented their places in the top three of the English premier league.
Liverpool stayed three points clear at the top of the table after goals from Stan Collymore and Michael Thomas secured a 2-1 win at West Ham, their seventh win in a row in all competitions.

United also maintained their unbeaten home league record with a comfortable 2-0 victory over Spurs, both goals coming from Norwegian Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, to move into third position a point behind second-placed Arsenal.
Liverpool have relied heavily on new Czech arrival Patrik Berger for recent goals, but it was Collymore who set them on their way by firing him a low left-foot shot in only the third minute.
The striker, though, had departed with a knee injury by the time Thomas provided the winner seven minutes into the second-half, finishing a flowing passing movement with a shot into the far corner
West Ham had done their best to upset the leaders after Croatian Slaven Bilic equalised in the 14th minute with a header from a Michael Hughes corner.

Julian Dicks hit the crossbar, Hughes was just over with a stunning volley and giant Liverpool goalkeeper David James was forced to save at full stretch from Tony Cottee and Iain Dowie in a revival sparked by new Portuguese signing Hugo Porfirio.

The unheralded Solskjaer continued his startling contribution to United's effort by taking his tally to five goals, earning himself the man of the match award. His first goal after 38 minutes, from a long aerial ball by Ryan Giggs, was notable for a superb first touch followed by a well-timed shot.
His second, a right-foot curler into the far corner, was equally well-taken and merely added to his growing reputation at Old Trafford.
"It's incredible, I can't believe it," said Solskjaer, who admitted he had not expected to be in the first-team before December. "To hear 55,000 people chanting my name was unbelievable."
